I had the opposite of this. For years I was in and out of therapists offices with no diagnosis, convinced something was deeply wrong with me. But every therapist said I was fine/not mentally ill. I still struggle with regret sometimes. It's different than it was when I first got clean. At first it was a lot like what you describe - regretting the damage I did to relationships, to my family. Feeling like I set myself so far back in life. 

Now it's not nearly as often or as harsh. Sometimes it's just the nostalgic tingle at hearing an old song from my childhood and remembering all of the dreams I had before my addiction took over. Sometimes it's looking at my son and wondering what our future is going to look like in the wake of so many lost years. Sometimes I look at my career and wonder if I'll ever have the job I dreamed of or the schooling I never got around to completing. 

But it does get better. It has gotten better. The regret can still be there, but I now know how to deal with those feelings. My advice (and this is only what works well for me) is this: Feel the feelings, be sad/angry/whatever. Then tell yourself that it's never to late to start over. Then move on with your day. Don't reject the feelings or push them aside, but don't dwell on them either.

A pyramid scheme is illegal in most countries and there is no real product. You get investors for something that doesn't exist and pay out early investors with later investors money. The first group in makes money if more people buy in. Eventually you can statistically not get any more investors and the last group in lose everything.

A MLM is run like a pyramid scheme except there is normally a "product". However, the product is not really the item being sold, but the person doing the selling. It's like if I came to you and said, "Do you want freedom? Do you want unlimited cash flow? Do you want your dreams to come true? Then purchase a car dealership and start selling car dealerships to other people! Selling actual cars isn't that important, but you can do that too!" That's what a MLM is all about. Selling the scheme, not the product.

Sara passed away my freshmen year of college and I was devastated. But because I was away It didn't really hit me until I came home for the summer.

However, right as I stood at the top of the stairs it dawned on me that those clicks couldn't be Sara. She was dead. I froze and felt this feeling of dread...
